candidates.original_title: Automaticity of social behavior: Direct effects of trait construct and stereotype activation on action
candidates.description: Exposure to elderly-related words causes participants to walk more slowly
candidates.citation_sentence: Studies 1a and 1b use a paradigm developed by [4] to examine the behavioral consequences of an implicitly primed elderly stereotype.
candidates.notes: The prime main effect in Study 1a was not significant (p = .13), but the Self-Consciousness x Prime interaction was significant (p < .05). The combined analysis across both studies explicitly replicates Bargh et al. (1996).

candidates.original_title: Automaticity of social behavior: Direct effects of trait construct and stereotype activation on action
candidates.description: Exposure to elderly-related words causes participants to walk more slowly
candidates.citation_sentence: Studies 1a and 1b use a paradigm developed by [4] to examine the behavioral consequences of an implicitly primed elderly stereotype.
candidates.notes: The prime main effect in Study 1b approached significance (p = .09), and the Self-Consciousness x Prime interaction was significant (p = .01). The combined analysis across both studies explicitly replicates Bargh et al. (1996).

candidates.original_title: Automaticity of social behavior: Direct effects of trait construct and stereotype activation on action
candidates.description: Exposure to an elderly stereotype prime causes participants to walk more slowly than participants exposed to a neutral prime.
candidates.citation_sentence: In a modern classic, Bargh, Chen, and Burrows (1996) demonstrated that implicit priming of stereotypes can bias an individual’s behavior in a stereotype-congruent manner even though the individual remains unaware of both the stereotype activation and its association to his or her own behavior.
candidates.notes: Study 1a used the elderly stereotype scrambled-sentence paradigm from Bargh et al. (1996) with an intervening lexical decision task. The interaction was significant, although the simple high-self-consciousness comparison was significant only with the authors' less-preferred post hoc test.

candidates.original_title: Automaticity of social behavior: Direct effects of trait construct and stereotype activation on action
candidates.description: Exposure to an elderly stereotype prime causes participants to walk more slowly than participants exposed to a neutral prime.
candidates.citation_sentence: In a modern classic, Bargh, Chen, and Burrows (1996) demonstrated that implicit priming of stereotypes can bias an individual’s behavior in a stereotype-congruent manner even though the individual remains unaware of both the stereotype activation and its association to his or her own behavior.
candidates.notes: Study 1b replicated the elderly-prime walking paradigm in a public community walkway with community pedestrians and no intervening task. Studies 2–4 were extensions of the authors' own work rather than qualifying replications of separately published original studies.
